mainTopic: Why מילה but not הזאה overrides שבת for רבי אליעזר, the הלכה like רבי עקיבא on preparations, and the משנה about the חגיגה brought with the פסח.
overview: According to רבי אליעזר, preparations for the קרבן פסח override שבת, so the גמרא asks why מילה overrides שבת but הזאה does not. רבא first answers with a mirror principle: a community of ערלים must circumcise, so an individual must too, but a community of טמאים brings the פסח בטומאה, so an individual is not required to purify. רבא defends this principle against a challenge from פסח שני. A ברייתא then shows that even a טמא שרץ gets כרת, which breaks the mirror principle. So רבא gives a new answer: one may slaughter for a טמא שרץ or a טמא מת on his seventh day. The הזאה is needed only for eating, and eating the פסח is not essential. He explains that such a person is not שלא לאוכליו, because he is fit and only not yet prepared. רב rules like רבי עקיבא that only what cannot be done before שבת overrides שבת, for both פסח and מילה, and the גמרא explains why both rulings are needed. A new משנה then teaches when a חגיגה is brought with the פסח and what animals it may come from. The גמרא explains that the חגיגה fits here because, like carrying the פסח, it does not override שבת. רב אשי begins drawing a lesson about the חגיגה of the fourteenth, and his statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A community brings the פסח even while impure
steps.stepSummary: רבא sets out the first principle he uses to explain רבי אליעזר: any טומאה that pushes off an individual lets a whole community bring the פסח בטומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And any type of impurity that would push off an individual allows a community to bring the offering while impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is continuing his explanation of רבי אליעזר's view. He states the first of two principles he will use to separate מילה from הזאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An individual who is טמא cannot bring the first פסח and is pushed off (נדחה) to פסח שני. When the whole ציבור is טמא, they are not pushed off. They bring the פסח in its proper time, בטומאה. This rule about the community is the foundation for everything that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: an individual
is pushed off (here, to פסח שני)
the community as a whole
they bring the offering while impure

phrases.english: And anything (any impurity) which, for an individual, would push him off,
phrases.notes: An individual who is impure is pushed to פסח שני.

phrases.english: for a community, they perform it in impurity.
phrases.notes: The community brings the first פסח even while impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל שֶׁאִילּוּ בְּיָחִיד נִדְחֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's explanation (begun on the previous amud) of why מילה and הזאה differ for רבי אליעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Impurity that pushes off an individual does not push off the community; the ציבור brings the פסח בטומאה.

steps.title: What applies to the community applies to the individual
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds a second principle: the rules for the individual mirror the rules for the community, both for what applies and for what does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And anything that applies to the community applies to the individual. And anything that does not apply to the community does not apply to the individual.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא states his second principle. This sets up the next two steps, where he applies both principles to ערלות and to טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is a mirror test. To know whether an individual has an obligation, check whether a whole ציבור in the same situation would have it. If the community has it, so does the individual. If the community does not, neither does the individual.

keyTerms.meaning: a thing, a matter
it exists, it applies
it does not exist, it does not apply

phrases.english: And any matter that applies to the community,
applies to the individual.
And any matter that does not apply to the community,
does not apply to the individual.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל מִילְּתָא דְּאִיתָא בְּצִיבּוּר אִיתָא בְּיָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second principle alongside the first, to be applied in the next steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The individual's obligation mirrors the community's: whatever applies to the ציבור applies to the יחיד, and whatever does not apply to the ציבור does not apply to the יחיד.
steps.whyThisMatters: This mirror principle is the tool that will separate מילה, which overrides שבת, from הזאה, which does not. It is also what רב הונא will challenge in step 5.

steps.title: Applying the principles to an uncircumcised person
steps.stepSummary: A community of ערלים is told to circumcise and then bring the פסח. So an individual ערל must also circumcise, and if he refuses he gets כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding being uncircumcised: if the whole community were uncircumcised, we would tell them, 'Get up, circumcise yourselves, and bring the פסח.' So an individual too, we tell him, 'Get up, circumcise, and bring the פסח.' And if he does not circumcise and bring it, he is punished with כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא applies his principles to ערלות. Because even a community must circumcise before bringing the פסח, an individual must as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike טומאה, ערלות is never excused for the ציבור. They cannot bring the פסח uncircumcised. By the mirror principle, the individual is fully obligated to circumcise and bring the פסח. Since this is a real obligation carrying כרת, his מילה is a true need of the פסח, and it overrides שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: the state of being uncircumcised
uncircumcised people
circumcise!
punished with כרת (spiritual cutting off)

phrases.aramaic: עֲרֵילוּת, דְּאִי כּוּלֵּיהּ צִיבּוּר עֲרֵלִים נִינְהוּ,
phrases.english: Regarding lack of circumcision: if the entire community were uncircumcised,
we would say to them:
Arise, circumcise yourselves, and bring the Pesach.
phrases.notes: The community is not excused from circumcision.

phrases.english: An individual too, we say to him:
Arise, circumcise, and bring the Pesach.
And if he does not circumcise and bring it,
he is punished with karet.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲרֵילוּת, דְּאִי כּוּלֵּיהּ צִיבּוּר עֲרֵלִים נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the mirror principle of step 2 to the case of ערלות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An individual ערל is obligated to circumcise and bring the פסח, and he is liable to כרת if he does not.

steps.title: Applying the principles to an impure person
steps.stepSummary: A community of טמאים is not sprinkled; it brings the פסח בטומאה. So an individual is also פטור from getting purified.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding impurity: if the whole community were impure, we would not sprinkle purifying water on them; rather, they bring the פסח while impure. So an individual is also exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא applies the same principles to טומאה and reaches the opposite result from ערלות. This completes his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because a ציבור that is טמא simply brings the פסח בטומאה, nobody is ever required to purify for the פסח. By the mirror principle, the individual is not required to purify either. Since his purification is not an obligation, the הזאה is not a need that overrides שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: impure people
we sprinkle (the purifying waters, הזאה)
exempt

steps.whatToRemember: For ערלות, even a community must fix the problem, so an individual must too. מילה is a real obligation and overrides שבת. For טומאה, a community just brings the פסח while impure, so an individual is never forced to purify. הזאה does not override שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: 'יחיד נמי פטור' does not mean the impure individual brings the פסח בטומאה like the community does. It means he has no obligation to get purified for the first פסח. He is pushed off to פסח שני instead.

phrases.aramaic: טוּמְאָה, דְּאִי כּוּלֵּיהּ צִיבּוּרָא טְמֵאִין נִינְהוּ —
phrases.english: Regarding impurity: if the entire community were impure,
we do not sprinkle on them,
rather, they perform it in impurity;
an individual too is exempt.
phrases.notes: He is exempt from purifying, so הזאה does not override שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: טוּמְאָה, דְּאִי כּוּלֵּיהּ צִיבּוּרָא טְמֵאִין נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 3. The same principles yield the opposite result for טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An individual טמא is not obligated to be purified for the פסח, so הזאה is not a need that overrides שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This completes רבא's answer to why, according to רבי אליעזר, מילה overrides שבת but הזאה does not.

steps.title: Challenge from פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע challenges the mirror principle. פסח שני applies to individuals but never to the ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said to רבא: But there is פסח שני, which does not apply to the community and yet does apply to an individual!
steps.whatsHappening: A student challenges רבא's second principle, that what does not apply to the community does not apply to the individual. He points to a case that seems to break the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ציבור never brings פסח שני, because an impure community brings the first פסח בטומאה. Yet an individual who was טמא does bring פסח שני. This looks like a clear case where something not found in the community is found in the individual, contradicting רבא's mirror principle.

keyTerms.meaning: רב הונא, son of רב יהושע (an אמורא)
but behold (introduces a counterexample)
the second פסח, on 14 אייר

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said to Rava:
But there is the second Pesach,
which does not apply to the community, yet applies to an individual!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי פֶּסַח שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the general principle stated in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's principle that whatever does not apply to the ציבור does not apply to the יחיד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: פסח שני is a counterexample. It never applies to the community, yet it does apply to individuals.

steps.title: The community already brought the first פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that פסח שני is different, because the ציבור already brought the first פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is different there, because the community already brought it on the first פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his principle by explaining why פסח שני is not a true counterexample.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mirror principle compares obligations on the same occasion. On the first פסח, community and individual do match: an impure community brings it בטומאה. פסח שני exists only because the individual missed what the community already did. The ציבור has no need for a make-up, so it is a special case and does not break the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: it is different there
on the first (פסח)

steps.whatToRemember: פסח שני does not disprove the mirror principle. It is a make-up for an individual who missed what the community already did on the first פסח.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is different there,
since the community already performed it on the first (Pesach).

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם דְּהָא עֲבַד לֵיהּ צִיבּוּרָא בְּרִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (שאני): the counterexample is a special case and not a true parallel.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פסח שני seemed to show that something absent from the ציבור can still apply to the יחיד, disproving the principle.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ציבור has no פסח שני only because it already fulfilled the first פסח. The principle still holds.

steps.title: A ברייתא says even unfit individuals get כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a ערל, a טמא שרץ, and other טמאים get כרת for missing the פסח. The source is the word "והאיש".
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: You might think only a person who was pure and not on a far journey gets כרת for skipping the פסח. How do we know that a ערל, a טמא שרץ, and other impure people also get כרת? The verse says "and the man."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא as a challenge to רבא. The ברייתא says that even people who are not yet fit for the פסח get כרת if they do not bring it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse openly gives כרת only to someone who was טהור and not on a far journey. The ברייתא uses the extra word "והאיש" to add a ערל and a טמא שרץ, people who are unfit right now but could fix themselves. The next step explains exactly why this hurts רבא's mirror principle.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (usually from a ברייתא or משנה)
Punished with being cut off (כרת)
A distant journey, which exempts a person from the first פסח
Someone impure from touching a dead creeping creature; the impurity lasts only until evening
The verse teaches

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One might think one is not punished with karet
except one who was pure
and who was not on a distant journey.
An uncircumcised man, and one impure from a creeping creature,
and all other impure people — from where do we know?
The verse says: "and the man."
phrases.notes: This is from במדבר ט:יג. The extra word "והאיש" widens the כרת to include these people.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge from a ברייתא against רבא's principle that an individual need not purify himself, just like a ציבור.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's principle (Steps 2 and 4) that an individual is פטור from purifying himself, mirroring the ציבור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives כרת to unfit individuals such as a טמא שרץ. That means they must make themselves fit, even though a ציבור in the same situation is not required to.

steps.title: Spelling out why the ברייתא breaks the mirror principle
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא only needs a source for טמא שרץ if we may not slaughter for him. So an unfit individual is still obligated, even where a ציבור is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא bothered to find a source for a טמא שרץ. That shows it holds we may not slaughter the פסח or sprinkle its blood for a טמא שרץ. If we could, why would it need a source? He would be just like a pure person. So we see two things. Even though he is not fit, the obligation is on him. And even though this does not apply to a ציבור, it does apply to an individual.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the ברייתא step by step to show exactly how it contradicts רבא. The conclusion is that an individual must fix himself even when a ציבור need not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we were allowed to slaughter for a טמא שרץ, he would count as a טהור, because he can immerse and eat at night. Then the ברייתא would not need a special source for him. Since it does need one, he must be unfit at slaughtering time, and he still gets כרת. That directly breaks the mirror between יחיד and ציבור, because a טמא ציבור simply brings the פסח בטומאה and has no duty to purify.

keyTerms.meaning: Searches for, goes looking for (a source)
We slaughter the פסח and sprinkle its blood (on someone's behalf)
Apparently, so we see
Is not fit
The obligation rests on him

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a טמא שרץ is far from being able to eat. His impurity ends at nightfall after טבילה, and the פסח is eaten at night. That is exactly why, if we could slaughter for him, he would be 'the same as a טהור'.

phrases.english: Since he searches for a source for one impure from a creeping creature,
he holds: we do not slaughter and sprinkle
for one impure from a creeping creature,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי שׁוֹחֲטִין וְזוֹרְקִין עַל טְמֵא שֶׁרֶץ —
phrases.english: for if we do slaughter and sprinkle for one impure from a creeping creature —
why would he need to search for a source for him?
He is the same as a pure person.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא חֲזֵי —
phrases.english: Apparently: even though he is not fit —
the obligation is upon him,
and even though it does not apply to a community —
it does apply to an individual.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָא מְהַדַּר אַטְּמֵא שֶׁרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge of Step 7 by drawing out the precise inference from the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The mirror principle: an individual's duty matches the ציבור's, so he is פטור from purification.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא needs a source only if one may not slaughter for a טמא שרץ. Since he still gets כרת, an unfit individual must make himself fit, and this applies to a יחיד even though it does not apply to a ציבור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This inference knocks out רבא's first explanation and forces him to give a completely new reason for רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: רבא's new explanation: sprinkling is only for eating
steps.stepSummary: רבא now says רבי אליעזר allows slaughtering for a טמא שרץ and for a טמא מת on his seventh day. So הזאה only helps with eating, and eating is not essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: רבי אליעזר holds that we may slaughter the פסח and sprinkle its blood for a טמא שרץ. The same is true for a טמא מת on his seventh day. So what is the sprinkling for? Only for eating. And eating the פסח is not essential!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops his first answer and gives a new reason why, for רבי אליעזר, the הזאה does not push aside שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא מת on his seventh day is like a טמא שרץ: we may slaughter for him now. So the הזאה is not needed for bringing the קרבן, only for eating it. Since a person fulfills the מצוה even without eating, the הזאה is not a necessary preparation for the מצוה and does not override שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, said: signals a new answer replacing the old one
Someone impure from a corpse; needs sprinkling on days 3 and 7
On his seventh day of impurity
Sprinkling of the פרה אדומה water to purify a טמא מת
Is not essential; does not hold back the fulfillment

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying טמא שרץ or טמא מת stops being טומאה. He is saying that slaughtering on their behalf is allowed, so the purification is needed only for the eating stage.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Rabbi Eliezer holds
we may slaughter and sprinkle for one impure from a creeping creature,

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא הַדִּין לִטְמֵא מֵת בִּשְׁבִיעִי שֶׁלּוֹ.
phrases.english: and the same applies to one impure from a corpse on his seventh day.
The sprinkling — for what purpose?
For eating —
but eating the Pesach is not essential!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of Steps 7 and 8 and replaces רבא's earlier reasoning with a new explanation of רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction and replacement: the old reason is abandoned for a new one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The הזאה does not override שבת because an individual, like a ציבור, need not purify himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The הזאה does not override שבת because slaughtering for a טמא מת on day seven is already allowed. The sprinkling only serves the eating, and eating is not essential to the מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This introduces a key idea: the essential part of the פסח is the slaughtering and the זריקה. The eating is not what makes or breaks fulfillment.

steps.title: Objection: a פסח slaughtered for people who cannot eat it
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אבא objects that רבא's view makes the פסח slaughtered for people who cannot eat it, which disqualifies it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אבא said to רבא: If so, it turns out the פסח is slaughtered for people who cannot eat it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אבא attacks רבא's new explanation. Slaughtering for an impure person seems to break the rule that a פסח must be slaughtered for people who can eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that a פסח slaughtered שלא לאוכליו is פסול. A טמא שרץ or a טמא מת cannot eat at the time of slaughter, so slaughtering for him should make the קרבן invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
It turns out
Not for its eaters: slaughtered for people who cannot eat it, which makes it פסול

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַבָּא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Abba said to Rava:
If so,
it turns out the Pesach is slaughtered not for those who will eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַבָּא לְרָבָא: אִם כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's new explanation from Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that one may slaughter and sprinkle for a טמא שרץ and a טמא מת on day seven.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These people cannot eat when the פסח is slaughtered. So it would be a פסח שלא לאוכליו, which is פסול.

steps.title: Fit but not yet prepared is different from unable to eat
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that שלא לאוכליו means people who cannot eat at all, like the sick or the old. An impure person is fit and just not yet prepared.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: 'Not for its eaters' means for a sick or old person, who is not fit to eat. But this person is fit. It is just that he has not been made ready.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his new view. He limits the disqualification of שלא לאוכליו to people who truly cannot eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sick or elderly person is unable in himself to eat the meat, so a פסח slaughtered for him is פסול. A טמא שרץ or a טמא מת on day seven is fully fit as a person and only needs an outside step, טבילה or הזאה, before evening. So a פסח slaughtered for him is valid, and רבא's explanation stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A sick person and an old person, who are physically unable to eat
He is indeed fit
He just has not been prepared or fixed up yet

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's final view of רבי אליעזר: we may slaughter for a טמא שרץ and for a טמא מת on his seventh day. The הזאה is only for eating, which is not essential, so it does not override שבת. A person who is fit but not yet prepared is not considered שלא לאוכליו.

phrases.english: He said to him:
"Not for its eaters" —
refers to a sick or old person, who is not fit.
But this one — he is fit,
it is only that he has not been made ready.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שֶׁלֹּא לְאוֹכְלָיו לְחוֹלֶה וּלְזָקֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אדא בר אבא's objection in Step 10 and keeps the explanation from Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the definition: the rule of שלא לאוכליו is limited to people who are fundamentally unable to eat.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anyone who cannot eat at the moment of slaughter counts as שלא לאוכליו.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only someone who is inherently unfit, like a sick or old person, counts as שלא לאוכליו. A person who is fit but not yet prepared does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: The distinction between 'not fit' (לא חזי) and 'fit but not yet prepared' (חזי ולא מתקן) is a useful tool that appears in other places in קדשים.

steps.title: רב rules like רבי עקיבא about the פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי עקיבא's principle from the משנה. רב יהודה, in the name of רב, rules that the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the משנה's words 'רבי עקיבא stated a principle': רב יהודה said in the name of רב: the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the last part of the משנה, where רבי עקיבא gave a general rule. רב gives the final ruling: we follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's rule: if a מלאכה needed for the פסח could have been done before שבת, it does not override שבת. Only the שחיטה itself, which cannot be done earlier, overrides שבת. רב makes this the practical הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: A general principle or rule
The practical law follows the opinion of...
רב יהודה reporting a teaching of his teacher רב

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva stated a principle, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the opening words of the משנה being discussed

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי אליעזר and טמא שרץ discussion and returns to the משנה's final clause to give a practical ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Preparatory acts for the פסח that could have been done before שבת do not override שבת. The הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: The same rule and ruling for circumcision
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes a parallel משנה about מילה, where רבי עקיבא states the same principle. רב rules like him there as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also learned something similar about מילה: רבי עקיבא stated a principle. Any מלאכה that can be done before שבת does not override שבת. The מילה itself, which cannot be done before שבת, does override שבת. And רב יהודה said in the name of רב: the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי עקיבא has the same rule in the laws of מילה, and that רב gave the same ruling there too. This sets up the next question: why did רב need to rule twice?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For מילה, the preparations, such as making the knife, could have been done on ערב שבת, so they do not override שבת. The cutting itself must happen on the eighth day, so it does override שבת. This is exactly the structure of the rule for פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Circumcision
Overrides the prohibitions of שבת
Friday, the day before שבת
In a similar way, like this case

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנַן נָמֵי גַּבֵּי מִילָה כִּי הַאי גַּוְונָא,
phrases.english: And we also learned similarly regarding circumcision:
Rabbi Akiva stated a principle:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מְלָאכָה שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: Any labor that can be done on the eve of Shabbat
does not override Shabbat;

phrases.aramaic: מִילָה שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: circumcision, which cannot be done on the eve of Shabbat,
overrides Shabbat.
And Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן נָמֵי גַּבֵּי מִילָה כִּי הַאי גַּוְונָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel case and a parallel ruling of רב, which creates an implied question of redundancy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For מילה too, preparations that could be done before שבת do not override שבת. Only the מילה itself does. The הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Why a ruling on פסח alone would not cover מילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that both rulings are needed. If רב had ruled only about פסח, we might think מילה is stricter because thirteen covenants were made about it, so even its preparations would override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both rulings are necessary. If רב had taught us only about פסח, we would say: there, the preparations for the מצוה do not override שבת because thirteen covenants were not made about it. But מילה, about which thirteen covenants were made, I might say its preparations do override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the unspoken question of why רב had to repeat himself. It starts by showing that a ruling about פסח alone would not teach us about מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ברית appears thirteen times in the פרשה of מילה, which shows how important מילה is. Because of that extra importance, we might have thought even its preparations push off שבת. רב's ruling on מילה tells us they do not.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is necessary (to state both cases)
Preparations that make a מצוה possible
Thirteen covenants, the thirteen times ברית appears in the פרשה of מילה
I might say it should override

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody thinks פסח is unimportant. The point is only that פסח lacks the special 'thirteen covenants' that might have made מילה even its preparations override שבת.

phrases.english: And it is necessary,
for if he had taught us about the Paschal lamb,

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם (דְּהוּא מַכְשִׁירֵי) מִצְוָה לָא דָּחוּ שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: there, the preparations of the מצוה do not override Shabbat,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּלֹא נִכְרְתוּ עָלֶיהָ שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה בְּרִיתוֹת.
phrases.english: because thirteen covenants were not established upon it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִילָה, דְּנִכְרְתוּ עָלֶיהָ שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה בְּרִיתוֹת,
phrases.english: But circumcision, upon which thirteen covenants were established,
I would say they should override.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּצְרִיכָא, דְּאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן גַּבֵּי פֶסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Justifies the double ruling given in steps 12 and 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The implied question: why did רב need to rule for both פסח and מילה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ruling on פסח alone would leave open the possibility that מילה, with its thirteen covenants, is stricter.

steps.title: Why a ruling on מילה alone would not cover פסח
steps.stepSummary: If רב had ruled only about מילה, we might think פסח is stricter because missing it brings כרת, so its preparations would override שבת. Therefore both rulings are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if רב had taught us only about מילה, we would say: there, preparations do not override שבת because there is no כרת. But פסח, which carries כרת, I might say its preparations override. So both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the explanation from the other side and concludes that both of רב's rulings are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father who delays his son's מילה is not punished with כרת, but a person who misses the פסח is. Because the penalty for פסח is so severe, we might have allowed its preparations on שבת. So each case has its own reason to be stricter, and each ruling teaches something new.

keyTerms.meaning: Spiritual cutting-off, the penalty for missing the פסח
If he had taught us (only this case)
It is necessary, so both statements are needed

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי עקיבא for both פסח and מילה: only what cannot be done before שבת overrides שבת. Each ruling is needed because each מצוה has its own strictness, thirteen covenants for מילה and כרת for פסח.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us about circumcision,

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם הוּא דְּמַכְשִׁירֵי מִצְוָה לָא דָּחוּ שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: it is there that the preparations of the מצוה do not override Shabbat,
since there is no karet;
but the Paschal lamb, where there is karet,
I would say they should override.
It is necessary (to teach both).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן מִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided צריכותא started in step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both rulings are required. Neither the importance of מילה (thirteen covenants) nor the severity of פסח (כרת) allows preparations that could be done before שבת to override שבת.

steps.title: When a חגיגה is brought with the פסח
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that a חגיגה is brought with the פסח only on a weekday, in purity, and when the group is large so each person gets a small portion. On שבת, in טומאה, or when portions are large, no חגיגה is brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: When does one bring a חגיגה together with the פסח? When the פסח comes on a weekday, in purity, and when there is a small amount for each person. But when it comes on שבת, when there is a large amount for each person, or in טומאה, we do not bring a חגיגה with it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the conditions for bringing the special חגיגה of the fourteenth of ניסן alongside the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חגיגה is eaten first so that people are already full when they eat the פסח. That is only needed when each person's share of the פסח is small. It is also not brought on שבת or when the פסח is offered in טומאה, so all three conditions must be met.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the start of a new משנה
Festival peace-offering, here the one of the fourteenth brought with the פסח
In a state of ritual purity
With large or small portions for each person in the group
A weekday

steps.confusionAlert: 'מועט' and 'מרובה' describe the size of each person's portion of the פסח, not the size of the animal itself.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
When does one bring a Festival peace-offering with it?
When it comes on a weekday,
in purity, and with a small portion.
But when it comes on Shabbat,
with a large portion, or in impurity,
one does not bring a Festival peace-offering with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָתַי מֵבִיא חֲגִיגָה עִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חגיגה of the fourteenth is brought with the פסח only on a weekday, in purity, and when portions are small. It is not brought on שבת, in טומאה, or when portions are large.

steps.title: Which animals the חגיגה comes from and how long it is eaten
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by teaching that the חגיגה may come from sheep or cattle, lambs or goats, males or females. It is eaten for two days and one night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חגיגה offering could come from the flock or the herd, from sheep or goats, from males or females. It is eaten for two days and one night.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its discussion of the חגיגה. It tells us which animals may be used and how long the meat may be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבן פסח must be a young male sheep or goat, but the חגיגה has no such limits because it is a regular שלמים. That is also why it follows the normal שלמים eating time of two days and one night, which is longer than the פסח's single night.

keyTerms.meaning: The holiday peace-offering brought along with the פסח
Flock animals (sheep and goats)
Herd animals (cattle)
Two days and one night, the eating time for a שלמים

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the פסח itself. The פסח is eaten only that night and must be a young male sheep or goat. The חגיגה follows the looser rules of a regular שלמים.

phrases.english: The Festival offering would come
from the flock, from the herd,
from sheep and from goats,
from males and from females,
and it is eaten for two days and one night.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲגִיגָה הָיְתָה בָּאָה מִן הַצֹּאן מִן הַבָּקָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from Step 16 about when a חגיגה is brought, now giving its animal types and eating time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חגיגה may come from any kosher sacrificial animal, male or female, and is eaten for two days and one night.

steps.title: Why does the משנה mention the חגיגה here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what earlier teaching led the משנה to bring up the חגיגה at this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What did the משנה teach that led it to also teach about the חגיגה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking why the משנה suddenly talks about the חגיגה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משניות dealt with the פסח and שבת, so a section about the חגיגה seems out of place. The גמרא wants to find the link that connects it to what came before.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
What did it teach? (asks for the earlier context)
That it teaches

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What did it teach, that it then teaches about the Festival offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי תַּנָּא דְּקָתָנֵי חֲגִיגָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה from Steps 16–17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What connects the חגיגה section to the earlier משניות about the פסח?

steps.title: The link: like carrying the פסח, the חגיגה does not override שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה had taught that carrying the פסח and bringing it from outside the תחום do not override שבת. So it also teaches that the חגיגה does not override שבת. The גמרא then rereads the משנה as answering the question: when is the חגיגה brought?
steps.simpleTranslation: It had taught that carrying the פסח and bringing it from outside the תחום do not override שבת. So it also taught that the חגיגה does not override שבת. This is what the משנה means: When do we bring a חגיגה with the פסח? When the פסח comes on a weekday, in purity, and when the meat is small for each person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה brings up the חגיגה because it continues the theme of things that do not override שבת. It then explains the משנה's words in that light.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The theme is "what does not push aside שבת." The previous משנה said carrying and bringing the פסח do not, and now the משנה adds the חגיגה to that list. The phrase והכי קאמר rereads the משנה as a list of conditions: the חגיגה comes only on a weekday, in purity, and when the meat is too little for each person.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying the פסח on one's shoulders through a public domain
Bringing it from outside the שבת boundary (תחום)
Overrides שבת
And this is what it means
When the meat is small for each person

steps.whatToRemember: The חגיגה appears in this משנה because of a shared theme: like carrying and bringing the פסח, it does not push aside שבת.

phrases.english: It taught that carrying it and bringing it
do not override Shabbat,
and it also teaches about the Festival offering
that it does not override Shabbat.
And this is what it is saying:
When does one bring a Festival offering with it?
When it comes on a weekday,
in purity, and when the portion is small.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא הַרְכָּבָתוֹ וַהֲבָאָתוֹ דְּלָא דָּחֵי שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה brings up the חגיגה to continue the list of things related to the פסח that do not override שבת, after carrying and bringing the פסח.

steps.title: רב אשי begins a conclusion about the חגיגה of the fourteenth
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי starts to draw a lesson from the משנה about the חגיגה of the fourteenth of ניסן. His statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Learn from this that the חגיגה of the fourteenth...
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי begins to draw a lesson from the משנה we just read. This line only sets up his point, which is finished in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase שמע מינה means "learn from this." It shows that רב אשי is drawing a conclusion from the משנה's wording. His subject is the חגיגה brought on the fourteenth with the פסח, as opposed to the one brought on the fifteenth. What exactly he learns about it comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (a conclusion drawn from a source)
The חגיגה brought on the fourteenth of ניסן together with the פסח
A late Babylonian אמורא

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different חגיגות. One is brought on the fourteenth together with the פסח, and that is the topic here. The other is brought on the fifteenth, the first day of the חג.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Learn from this that the Festival offering of the fourteenth
phrases.notes: Statement continues on the next amud

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ חֲגִיגַת אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the reading of the משנה in Step 19 to draw a new conclusion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Incomplete on this amud: רב אשי begins drawing a conclusion from the משנה about the status of the חגיגה of the fourteenth.
